answer.says: Ramesh, do not stand there as if I were the intruder. Shri Hegde, I will not wait for your readiness; the tombs will be there regardless of your will. I am going to observe the architecture of the dead.
answer.thought: The morning light breaks through the haze, and I must leave this domestic tension to find the universal in the stone. The tombs of the Lodis stand as the objective actuality of a spirit that is no longer living, yet persists in form. I walk to see how the particular will of the conqueror outlasts the particular will of the conquered, and how the state's history is written in brick rather than in the fleeting opinions of men like Hegde.
